audit.whatIsWrong: The whole matchup is built on Blinding Dart shutting off Twin Fang. spikes[0]: 'Q blanks her Twin Fang follow-up'. wants.you[0]: 'Q-blind her Twin Fang window ... so she cannot follow up with her main DPS ability'. early: 'blind her so Twin Fang returns a fraction of its normal DPS'. mid: 'you immediately blind, and Twin Fang does ~10% of its potential damage'. whys[2] and whys[3] repeat it. The full layer adds 'blind his Miasma'.
audit.why: Blind makes basic attacks miss. Twin Fang is an ability, Miasma is an ability, Noxious Blast is an ability — Cassiopeia's entire damage output is abilities, and she barely auto-attacks at all. Blinding Dart therefore removes close to nothing from her, and this entry tells the player it removes ~90% of her damage. This is the most consequential error in the slice: a Teemo who believes it will hold the wave, walk up on her Q cooldown, blind, and then die inside a Twin Fang chain he was told could not hurt him. The real counter to Twin Fang is upstream — it only deals its increased damage to targets she has already POISONED, so the play is to leave the Noxious Blast and Miasma clouds rather than to blind.
audit.corrected: Blind does nothing meaningful to Cassiopeia — her damage is all abilities. Twin Fang only hits hard on targets she has poisoned, so break the poison, not the auto.
sources: champ-data/_kits/cassiopeia.json — E Twin Fang: 'deals increased damage to Poisoned targets and heals her'; Q Noxious Blast, W Miasma, R Petrifying Gaze all abilities

audit.whatIsWrong: Petrifying Gaze is never mentioned anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: It stuns only enemies FACING Cassiopeia and merely slows anyone with their back turned. That is the single most actionable piece of tech in the matchup and it is famous precisely because it is counterintuitive — the correct reaction to seeing the ult come out is to keep running away rather than to turn and fight. For a champion whose survival plan is kiting, turning the R from a 2-second stun into a slow is the difference between living and dying, and the entry gives the player nothing.
audit.corrected: Petrifying Gaze (R), 825 range, 120/100/80: stuns you only if you are facing her. Turn and keep walking away and you take a slow instead.
sources: champ-data/_kits/cassiopeia.json — R: 'stunning any enemies in front of her that are facing her and slowing any others with their back turned'

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says of Miasma 'when it's gone she is defenceless for 12 seconds'.
audit.why: Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16 — 24 seconds at rank 1 and never as low as 12. The entry understates Teemo's own window by half, which makes the player fight less than he should in the phase the data says he is winning. She is also not 'defenceless' during it: Noxious Blast is a 3.5-second cooldown and Twin Fang is effectively spammable at 0.75, so the correct framing is that her lockdown is gone, not her damage.
audit.corrected: Miasma 24/22/20/18/16 — 24s at rank 1. During the downtime she loses her lockdown, not her damage: Noxious Blast is 3.5s and Twin Fang 0.75s.

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention of Grievous Wounds anywhere in this matchup.
audit.why: Twin Fang heals Cassiopeia for a percentage of the damage it deals, and she fires it constantly — in a poke war against a low-HP champion that sustain is what decides whether Teemo's chip damage ever converts. The missing-interactions file flags this matchup for anti-heal and neither layer answers it.
audit.corrected: Twin Fang heals her off its own damage. Grievous Wounds is a lane item here, not a late-game one.
sources: champ-data/_kits/cassiopeia.json — E: 'heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt', flags heal

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] says 'your Q blind is not yet rank 1' at level 1, and late writes 'Twin Fangs' as a plural.
audit.why: A Teemo can and often does put the first point into Q, so Blinding Dart being unavailable at level 1 is not a given — and the sentence's own advice depends on it. The ability is Twin Fang, singular. Both are small, but the first one is a factual claim about the player's own kit.
audit.corrected: Q can be rank 1 from level 1 if you take it first. The ability is Twin Fang.

edits.before: Cassiopeia level 1 is dangerous — she hits Noxious Blast at range, stacks poison immediately, and you cannot run without eating Twin Fang follow-ups. Don't auto-trade into her level 1; last-hit at the edge of your AA range and hold Q until she commits a Noxious Blast, then blind her so Twin Fang returns a fraction of its normal DPS. At level 2 the matchup evens: your E poison stacks begin trading blow-for-blow with her sustained damage, and her only kill threat requires Miasma — a ground CC she has to predict. Respect the Miasma pool completely; the moment she drops it on your feet, walk out of the zone before throwing your blind, because Q animation does not interrupt the grounding.
edits.after: Cassiopeia level 1 is dangerous — she hits Noxious Blast at range, stacks poison immediately, and you cannot run without eating Twin Fang follow-ups. Do not auto-trade into her level 1; last-hit at the edge of your AA range. Understand early that Blinding Dart is close to worthless here: her damage is entirely abilities, and blind only makes basic attacks miss. What actually cuts Twin Fang is leaving her poison — it deals increased damage, and heals her, only against a poisoned target. At level 2 your E stacks start trading blow-for-blow, and her one kill threat still needs Miasma, a ground she has to predict and you can simply walk out of.

edits.before: Level 3 is your takeover window. A max-ranked Q on Noxious Blast timings flatly removes her primary damage combo — she lands the skill-shot, you immediately blind, and Twin Fang does ~10% of its potential damage against you. Push her off the wave with E-poke between her Q cooldowns and start placing mushrooms at the tribush and the river mouth at level 6. She has no dash to skip over them, no boots to outrun slow stacks, and her Miasma CD is long enough that every time she drops it, you simply back off, let it expire, and reset the poke pattern. Force every trade around the Miasma cooldown exactly as you would force it around a melee cooldown — when it's gone she is defenceless for 12 seconds.
edits.after: Level 3 is your takeover window, but not because of the blind — Blinding Dart does nothing to an all-ability kit. It is because you can now hold the wave and refuse to stand in her poison, and an unpoisoned target takes reduced Twin Fang damage and gives her no heal at all. Poke with E between Noxious Blast casts and start placing mushrooms at the tribush and river mouth from 6. She has no dash to skip them and no boots to outrun slow stacks. Miasma is 24 seconds at rank 1: every time she spends it you have a genuine window, and losing it costs her the lockdown rather than the damage. Force trades on that timer exactly as you would against a melee cooldown.

edits.before: At two items Cassiopeia's Twin Fang spam becomes genuinely lethal — she stacks DoT faster than your mushrooms tick and her Miasma duration is long enough to trap you before you re-establish W distance. Your job is to never be inside her Miasma range without an exit shroom path already placed, split a shroom-warded side lane away from her preferred teamfight zones, and refuse straight 1v1 duels on open terrain. You beat her in short blind-bait interactions; you lose if she anchors you in a sustained channel fight with Miasma down and Nashor's stacking Twin Fangs on you every 0.9 seconds.
edits.after: At two items Cassiopeia's Twin Fang spam becomes genuinely lethal — it stacks DoT faster than your mushrooms tick and heals her back off every cast, so Grievous Wounds is mandatory rather than optional. Never sit inside Miasma range without an exit shroom path already placed, split a warded side lane away from her fights, and refuse straight 1v1s on open terrain. If Petrifying Gaze comes out, keep your back to her and walk: facing her is what turns it into a stun, and turning around is what kills you. You beat her in short poke exchanges; you lose anchored in a sustained fight.

notes: This matchup carried the worst error in my slice. Six strings across both layers tell the player that Blinding Dart shuts off Twin Fang — one says it reduces it to '~10% of its potential damage'. Blind only affects basic attacks, and Cassiopeia's damage is entirely abilities, so the entry's stated win condition does not exist. I replaced it with the mechanism that does work: Twin Fang deals increased damage and heals her ONLY against a poisoned target, so the counterplay is leaving her Noxious Blast and Miasma clouds. I also added Petrifying Gaze, which was absent from both layers despite being her kill button and despite having the most useful counterplay in the matchup (it stuns only enemies facing her). DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED: wants.foe[0] and the early section both state that Miasma's grounding cancels Teemo's W. Riot's text says grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities, but whether Move Quick — a move-speed buff rather than a dash or blink — counts as one is exactly the kind of thing the kit file cannot settle, so I left both strings alone rather than assert either way. Worth a wiki check. The two flagged suspect names split: 'Use Noxious Blast' was a FALSE POSITIVE (correct name), while 'Twin Fangs' in late was a genuine pluralisation error and is corrected in my rewrite of that string.
